config.title: usePrevious

intro.title: usePrevious
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React Hook called `usePrevious` that tracks and returns the previous value of a state or prop. You'll learn how to leverage the `useRef` and `useEffect` hooks to persist values across renders without triggering re-renders. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript, using functional components and hooks. By the end, you'll understand how to capture a value from a previous render and apply this pattern in your own projects.
intro.usecase: The usePrevious hook is essential in React applications where you need to compare current and previous values to detect meaningful changes. In dashboards, it helps track metric fluctuations by comparing current data points with previous ones to trigger alerts or visual highlights. In form workflows, it enables detecting when specific fields change to show validation messages or enable/disable submission buttons. It's also crucial in interactive UI components like sliders or filters where you need to respond only when values cross certain thresholds compared to their previous state.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook that tracks the previous value of a state variable
Apply TypeScript generics to create a type-safe usePrevious hook
Initialize and update a ref to store the previous value within the hook
Integrate the usePrevious hook into a functional component to monitor state changes
Render both current and previous values in the component's UI for comparison
Manipulate component state to observe the hook's behavior in real-time
Configure the hook to handle initial renders by returning undefined appropriately
